title: Reservoir Dogs
hint_1: A debut feature from a video store clerk who would go on to spend the next thirty years convincing audiences that talking about hamburgers is more interesting than the heist itself.
hint_2: The robbery happens entirely offscreen, which is either a stroke of minimalist genius or the result of a first-time director's budget meeting going very poorly.
hint_3: You've seen this. Color-coded aliases, a warehouse, a severed ear, and a Stuck in the Middle With You needle drop that ruined that song for polite company forever.
hint_4: Mr. White. Mr. Pink. Mr. Blonde. The title is two words — one is an animal, the other is a place you'd rather not be standing in a black suit.

title: Jackie Brown
hint_1: The 1997 follow-up to a certain pulpy two-hour conversation about feet and royale with cheese, this one slowed down, grew up, and let a 70s blaxploitation icon carry the whole thing on her shoulders.
hint_2: An Elmore Leonard adaptation about a flight attendant outsmarting a gunrunner, the ATF, and a beach-bum surfer played by a guy who normally plays beach-bum stoners.
hint_3: Either you haven't seen this, or you have and that's somehow worse — there's a shopping mall, a changing room, and a bag of cash that changes hands more times than a deck of cards in Vegas.
hint_4: Ordell. Louis. Max Cherry. A Delfonics song doing more emotional work than most actors manage in a career. The title is her name.

title: Kill Bill: Vol. 1
hint_1: A 2003 revenge fantasy so soaked in homage that it doubles as a graduate seminar in 1970s Japanese cinema, Hong Kong wirework, and anime interludes the studio probably didn't budget for.
hint_2: A yellow tracksuit, a katana forged by a sushi chef who swore off making swords, and a single fight scene with so many extras the production ran out of fake blood and had to switch to black-and-white.
hint_3: At this point I have to ask — does the phrase "Crazy 88" mean anything to you? A bride in a coma? A wiggling toe?
hint_4: The Bride. O-Ren Ishii. Vernita Green. The title is a command, a name, and the second half is what she plans to do to the title character.

title: Kill Bill: Vol. 2
hint_1: The 2004 second half of a story originally meant to be one film, until someone looked at the runtime and decided audiences would prefer to pay twice.
hint_2: This one trades the anime sequences and Tokyo nightclub massacre for a buried-alive sequence, a trailer in the desert, and a five-point exploding heart technique that does exactly what it sounds like.
hint_3: The fact that you're still guessing tells me something about you — specifically that the words Pai Mei, eyeball plucking, and a flute-playing assassin in a Texas trailer park aren't ringing any bells.
hint_4: The Bride finally gets to the title character. He's played by the guy from Kung Fu. The title is the same as the first one, just with a number after it.

title: Death Proof
hint_1: A 2007 throwback to drive-in exploitation films, released as half of a double feature that nobody asked for and most theaters refused to show in full.
hint_2: A stuntman with a reinforced car uses it as a murder weapon, which is the kind of premise you come up with after spending too many afternoons watching Vanishing Point on VHS.
hint_3: I want you to think carefully about what you actually know — the film is half talky diner scenes and half a car chase so prolonged the stuntwoman is actually clinging to the hood for real.
hint_4: Stuntman Mike. A 1970 Dodge Challenger. The title refers to what the killer's car is, and what his victims very much are not.

title: The Hateful Eight
hint_1: A filmmaker who never met a monologue he didn't like decided to make a chamber piece western, set almost entirely inside one room, and shot it in 70mm anyway, because why not.
hint_2: A bounty hunter, his prisoner, a blizzard, a haberdashery, and a poisoned pot of coffee — the setup of a mystery novel, the runtime of a long-haul flight.
hint_3: Let me be direct with you — there's a number in the title, and it's the number of suspicious strangers stuck in a cabin waiting to find out who's lying.
hint_4: Daisy Domergue gets punched in the face roughly every nine minutes. The title is an adjective plus a number. The number is one more than seven.
